pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/glyph/CapabilitySigil.tsx:59 The context writes down the rule 'connected wrappers read, the primitive renders' and admits that no boundary gate reaches shared/glyph/. In the same directory, InteractiveSigil.tsx:9 still imports useThemeStore, and GlyphCard/GlyphQuestionPanel import other features. The forbidden action succeeds silently, which is prose-rule drift.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/glyph/InteractiveSigil.tsx:9 The store read that CapabilitySigil removed is still present in its sibling, and the comment above it cites CapabilitySigil as precedent. No census rule or ESLint rule covers glyph/, so nothing distinguishes this from compliance.

src/features/shared/glyph/triggers.ts:48 The per-kind icon table is checked against the generated TriggerKind identifier set at compile time, so a kind added in Rust cannot ship without a row and a stray key is an excess-property error.

src/features/shared/glyph/__tests__/glyphPrimitives.test.ts:159 The totality test reads its population from the independent TRIGGER_KINDS authority rather than from the map under test, so it can actually fail.

src/features/shared/glyph/cron.ts:9 The code names the lint rule's scope (JSX text only) instead of treating lint green as proof the strings were translated. The fix (taking t) does not rely on that gate.
